title: One commit on trunk: built once, tested, promoted, then turned on with a flag
captions: A developer merges a small pull request into main. It changes 60 lines. The new feature is inside a feature flag that is off.
The pipeline starts on its own. It builds the code once, from this exact commit.
Unit and integration tests run. They finish in 8 minutes, so the developer still remembers the change if something fails.
The pipeline packages the build into one image, app:a1b2c. It stores the image and signs it. Nobody builds it again.
The same image goes to staging. Smoke tests check that it starts and answers requests.
The same image goes to production, in stages. The flag is still off, so users see no change. Deploying code is not the same as releasing a feature.
The team turns the flag on for 1% of users and watches errors and latency. If they rise, they turn the flag off in seconds. If not, they go wider.
